metallurgy_verification.verdict: SOUND -- not refuted on any of the four mechanisms the brief named, nor on the six further claims this audit checked unprompted.
metallurgy_verification.fast_form_reduction: CORRECT. 'Jarnet reducerades i fast form: kolmonoxiden ur kolet drog syret ur malmkornen, och det som blev kvar bakades ihop till en klump som aldrig runnit nagonstans -- en seg, poros lupp, genomdragen av stelnad slagg.' This is the direct/bloomery process exactly: solid-state reduction of iron oxide by CO below the melting point of iron, yielding a spongy bloom with entrapped slag. 'kolmonoxiden ur kolet' is a permissible simplification (CO is generated from the charcoal carbon plus the blast, via C + O2 -> CO2 and CO2 + C -> 2CO); the carbon does come from the charcoal, so the phrase is not wrong, only compressed. The consequence the passage draws -- the bloom must be reheated and hammered repeatedly to expel slag -- is the standard account.
metallurgy_verification.temperature_pair: CORRECT AND WELL-CALIBRATED. 'Temperaturen i schaktet nadde omkring 1200 grader. Det racker for att smalta slaggen, men inte jarnet, som inte blir flytande forran langt over 1500 grader.' Pure iron melts at 1538 C, so 'langt over 1500' is right and correctly non-specific. Fayalitic bloomery slag (Fe2SiO4-dominated) has a liquidus near 1150-1200 C, so 1200 C melting the slag but not the metal is exactly the operating window of a bloomery. Adversarial probe: real bloomeries run hotter at the tuyere (1300-1400 C) than in the shaft body, but the passage says 'i schaktet' and hedges with 'omkring', so the figure is scoped correctly rather than overstated.
metallurgy_verification.carbon_embrittlement: CORRECT, and internally coherent with the temperature claim. 'De blasningar som drevs hardast, med tatare balgtag och mer kol i varven, gav inte storre luppar utan sprodare: kolet gick in i jarnet, och klumpen sprack under sladgan.' Harder blast plus a higher charcoal:ore ratio raises carbon pick-up; carburised iron is harder and more brittle and cracks rather than draws under the hammer. This is the well-known over-carburisation failure of over-driven bloomeries, and it is the mechanism by which a bloomery accidentally makes cast iron. Note the coherence the passage earns without stating it: carburised iron melts far below 1538 C (roughly 1150-1300 C at 2%+ C), i.e. within the shaft temperature the passage already gave -- so the two claims support each other rather than merely coexisting.
metallurgy_verification.iron_rich_slag_as_condition: CORRECT, and this is the strongest single claim in the piece. 'En slagg med lagre jarnhalt blir trogflytande vid de temperaturer en sadan ugn orkar halla; den rinner inte undan utan blir kvar kring kornen, och luppen gar da inte att rensa. Jarnet i avfallet ar priset for att slaggen alls ska lamna schaktet.' Fayalitic slag stays fluid at bloomery temperature precisely BECAUSE it is FeO-rich; lowering the iron fraction (raising silica/alumina) raises the liquidus and the viscosity, and the slag then fails to tap and stays around the reduced grains. Deliberate iron loss to slag is a recognised structural feature of the direct process, not a defect. The passage's re-framing of a 'loss' as a 'price' is archaeometallurgically standard and is the correct correction of the naive reading.
further_claims_checked_unprompted: Slag Fe fraction 'kring en tredjedel av vikten': fayalite is 54.8 % Fe by weight and bloomery slags typically run 40-60 % FeO, giving roughly 30-45 % Fe. ~33 % is squarely inside the real range. PLAUSIBLE.

Bog-ore formation: 'Jarnhaltigt grundvatten kan tranga fram i en mosse eller under en sjobotten' and grains 'artstora eller mindre' -- correct for myrmalm and sjomalm, and 'artmalm' (pea ore) is the attested Swedish term for exactly that grain size. CORRECT, and the P2 scoping repair ('i ett skikt som i mossen ligger under torven') is factually necessary, because there is no peat under a lake bed.

Preparation chain: frost-shattering over winter, rain washing out humus, then roasting on a wood bed to drive off moisture and organic matter and make the grains friable -- correct practice, and roasting additionally converts hydrated oxides to a more friable oxide. CORRECT.
Prospecting with a spett and reading the change of resistance under the peat -- correct field method for locating a myrmalm layer that does not show at the surface. CORRECT.

Hytta contrast: melts the iron, yields liquid pig iron, requires water power and continuous operation, and the pig iron must be farskat before it can be forged -- all correct, including the ordering that production moved from the parishes to the bruk only then. CORRECT.

Dating: 300s-1200s for Smaland bloomery iron, from charcoal in the tapping pits, with the caveat 'kolet ger arhundraden, inte artal'. Well calibrated to the real Swedish record (blast furnaces appear c. 1150-1300, so the upper bound is right at the transition) and the radiocarbon precision caveat is correct. CORRECT.

carried_items_weighed.g_register_lane_clone_major: RECORDED, NOT ADJUDICATED -- this is an OWNER-level call and the auditor declines it deliberately. The finding is real and I reproduce its factual base independently: the unit is the second consecutive LAS facktext-long built on a rural Swedish furnace craft, it is the fourth heat/fire craft in the last six long slots (las-b14-001 kolmilor/tjardalar, las-b16-001 tegelbruk, las-b18-001 kalkugnar, this), both of the back-to-back pair carry the furnace in the title, and the lane moves line up one for one -- a low clay/stone furnace in a named socken, a seasonal rhythm set by frost and firewood, a named researcher who has surveyed the remains in the landscape, an experimental reconstruction raised beside the excavated sites, remains read as a low mound with a hollow, a three-to-four-term craft glossary, and a coda that dates the practice. The family-exclusion list did not catch it because the declared family strings differ. I add one observation the gate did not make, in the unit's favour: the two units' PAYLOADS do not overlap at all -- b18-001 teaches a chemistry (burning then slaking) and an economic organisation (the ugnslag), this one teaches a physical constraint (solid-state reduction) and a counterintuitive re-reading of waste as precondition. A student who did both would learn two different things about two different processes; what repeats is the SETTING and the narrative frame, not the content. DISPOSITION PROPOSAL AS RECORDED BY G-REGISTER-r2, reproduced verbatim for the owner and not endorsed or ranked by this audit: (a) SHIP AS IS and bind batch20's LAS long brief to exclude every furnace/kiln/combustion craft and every experimental-reconstruction frame; (b) SHIP WITH SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT -- never place las-b18-001 and las-b19-001 in the same provpass or the same adaptive session; (c) REGENERATE the lane on a non-craft LAS long topic, the only option that actually reduces the four-in-six concentration, at the cost of a full generation and gate cycle. The audit's only addition is that option (b) is cheap, is enforceable in the assembly step, and is the one that addresses the finding's actual stated harm ('student-visible across a study session') without discarding a unit whose content is new.
carried_items_weighed.g_stem_q1_world_knowledge: REFUTED as a leak claim -- see F9. The G-STEM r1 record for q:1 states 'BLIND: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, pick=A' and reasons that 'Standard knowledge of myrmalm decides the pair: the ore was taken while the frost carried the mire.' The shipped key is C. The blind pick is therefore WRONG, which means the world-knowledge channel on q1 leads AWAY from the key rather than toward it -- the opposite of a leak. The underlying domain claim is also mistaken: myrmalm was dug in late summer or autumn when the water in the mire had dropped, then left out to be broken up by frost over the winter and roasted afterwards, which is precisely the passage's chain; harvesting from the ice belongs to SJOMALM (lake ore), and frozen-ground work in the myrmalm cycle is HAULAGE, not lifting. The passage is historically right and the gate's blind solver walked into the distractor the unit planted for exactly that reader. Held as a strength, not a residual.

Two channels are named: (i) domain -- knowing the direct process reduces in the solid state makes D true on its own terms, and knowing that water power belongs to the blast furnace strips B; (ii) form -- D is 'the only both-X-and-Y option, the usual shape of a which-statement-agrees-best key'. Channel (ii) does NOT survive a sheet-wide check: q1's key C is also a two-clause conjunction, and q4's DISTRACTOR D is the sheet's other 'X and Y' option, so the conjunction-shape heuristic scores 1 for 1 against, i.e. it is noise. Channel (i) also requires a student to know what 'reducerades i fast form' entails, which the passage itself has to explain -- if the reader already has it, the item is measuring nothing on this question, but that reader is rare in the target population. Held.
carried_items_weighed.g_stem_q4_world_knowledge: UPHELD in fact and DOWNGRADED in weight. The claim is correct -- fayalitic bloomery slag must stay iron-rich to run fluid, so an archaeometallurgist picks B blind. But the calibration question is whether the target population has that fact, and it does not: this is specialist archaeometallurgy, not school science, and it is exactly the fact the passage exists to teach. The other blind observations in the r3 record are better ones and I reproduce both: A strips on register alone (a blame-framed 'vardslos hantering' option is the standard distractor shape in this genre), and C is the only 'no conclusion available' option under a stem that asks for a conclusion. Those two are the real residual on q4 and they are form-level, not domain-level. Net: q4's blind floor is worse than q1's and better than q2's. Held.
carried_items_weighed.sextiotva_prover_spread: UPHELD as a soft joint, charged as F4, and explicitly NOT as an error. The passage reports 62 samples from 11 sites and then says the iron ran 'i flera fall kring en tredjedel av vikten', from which it concludes 'vilket betyder att mer jarn stannade i avfallet an som lamnade ugnen i luppen'. Two things are compressed there: an unquantified subset ('i flera fall' of 62) is generalised to the process, and a CONCENTRATION is converted into a MASS comparison without the slag:bloom mass ratio that the conversion needs -- the passage supplies that only obliquely and much later ('raknas varpen i ton', P9). Both steps are true in practice for bloomeries and neither is exposed by any question: q4's key rests on P7's two mechanism sentences, not on this arithmetic, and the passage's own argumentative move is to leave Krokvall's NUMBERS standing and attack her INFERENCE, which insulates the item further. Recorded because 'vilket betyder att' presents an inference as an entailment.
carried_items_weighed.residual_absolutizers_distractor_side: UPHELD as correctly carried, and I verified the carry reasoning rather than accepting it. Three remain, all distractor-side: q1 B 'varje', q2 C 'samtliga', q2 D 'allt' (the last a list false-positive on the fixed adverbial 'framfor allt'). The carry argument in fleet-repair-3 is that each sits in a question that still has a clean, absolutizer-free distractor, so strip-the-absolutes decides nothing -- and that is exactly what the recount shows: q1 goes 4->3 (A, C, D survive), q2 goes 4->2 and lands on the A/B mirror pair where the heuristic has no further purchase. q3 and q4 are clean throughout. M-FORM passes unchanged. Correctly carried.
carried_items_weighed.intra_batch_thesis_echo: CARRIED, disposition owned at elf-b19-001 as G-REGISTER recorded. Both of batch19's long units run the same adjudication -- a named male investigator's practical review concedes a named female incumbent's numbers and refutes her reading of them (Tolvsater/Krokvall; Calverend/Grendisham). I reproduce the observation and note one thing in this unit's defence that bears on the gender axis specifically: the unit was BUILT to invert the bank's 18-of-18 careful-woman/overconfident-man pattern and it does give Krokvall the serious version of her objection (62 samples, 11 sites, both varp and tapped cakes), so she loses on evidence rather than on characterisation. findings.disposition: FIX ORDERED (provenance metadata only; the name never reached the bytes, so this does not gate ship)
findings.claim: The law-16 log's most load-bearing rejection is recorded with a false reason. Gunnar Nybrant was not a metallurgist.
findings.evidence: Re-run 2026-09-01, same endpoint: sv.wiki exact "Nybrant" -> totalhits = 4, titles ['Gunnar Nybrant', '1 mars', '3 juli', 'Lista over ledamoter av Kungliga Vetenskapsakademien']; Nominatim se -> 0. The count, the bearer and the KVA membership reproduce exactly (KVA list entry 1132). The article lead reads 'Gunnar Levi Nybrant ... var en svensk hydrolog och meteorolog', and both date-page entries say 'svensk hydrolog och direktor'. His career is Uppsala meteorology, Lantbrukshogskolan, hydrograf at SMHA, forste statshydrolog 1948, byrachef 1957, expert on ice problems in Norway and Canada. No metallurgist bearer of 'Nybrant' appears anywhere in the result set.

What fails is the log's evidential value. A search log's whole purpose is that it can be replayed, and this entry cites the one fact that would have made the collision severe (same profession as the passage) when the real bearer's field is unrelated. It also mis-invokes the 2026-07-30 precedent, which is specifically about related-field collisions. This is the honesty spot-check the brief asked for and it lands as a partial refutation: the rejection reproduces, the reason does not. Fix: replace 'a real Swedish metallurgist and KVA member ... a related-field collision on exactly the profession this unit is about' with 'a real Swedish hydrologist and meteorologist, KVA member -- an UNRELATED-field collision, discarded anyway under the any-real-bearer rule', and drop the 2026-07-30 cross-reference. findings.stage_challenged: q2 rationale, distractor C (student-visible teaching payload)
findings.disposition: FIX RECOMMENDED (one clause; does not gate ship, does not touch key or options)
findings.claim: The q2 rationale refutes distractor C by asserting something the passage does not say. It reads: 'C ar overgeneralisation: texten talar om ett samre men ANVANDBART utfall, inte om att alla omgangar havererade sa snart driften okade.' The passage does not report a usable outcome for the hard-driven runs.
findings.evidence: The passage's only statement about those runs is 'De blasningar som drevs hardast, med tatare balgtag och mer kol i varven, gav inte storre luppar utan sprodare: kolet gick in i jarnet, och klumpen sprack under sladgan i stallet for att lata sig strackas.' A bloom that cracks under the sledge instead of drawing out is precisely the thing that cannot be worked into iron. What the passage DOES support is weaker: that blooms were still obtained ('gav ... luppar' presupposes a product) and that they were more brittle. 'Anvandbart' is the rationale's own addition and is contradicted in spirit by the cracking clause it is meant to gloss.
findings.why: The rationale is the item's teaching payload and a student reads it after answering; here it teaches a fact about the trials that the text does not carry, and it does so while explaining a distractor the student may well have chosen. The key is not threatened -- C dies cleanly on two other grounds that the rationale under-uses: the universal 'Samtliga' over 36 runs, and the threshold 'sa snart balgtagen blev tatare an VANLIGT' where the passage predicates only of the superlative subset 'De blasningar som drevs HARDAST'. Recommended replacement: 'C ar overgeneralisation: texten talar om de hardast drivna omgangarna, inte om alla, och den sager inte att de havererade -- luppar bildades, men de var sprodare och sprack under sladgan.' Note that two G-KEY legs independently reached the same reading ('the hard runs produced lumps, they were merely brittle'), which is defensible; the shipped rationale's 'anvandbart' goes one step past it.

findings.disposition: HELD -- real residual, family-typical, carried per batch calibration policy; recorded at minor rather than dismissed
findings.claim: q2 retains a genuine passage-independent path to the key that is available to the ACTUAL target population, not only to a specialist. The unit's declared adversarial blind floor for q2 ('1-in-2 at best') is therefore optimistic.
findings.evidence: Three steps, none requiring the passage: (i) A and B are exact mirrors on one variable, so the key is one of them and the field is 2; (ii) 'more carbon in iron makes it more brittle' is gymnasium-level Swedish chemistry/teknik (gjutjarn brittle, stal tough, kolhalt the difference), and it decides the pair for A; (iii) A is additionally the only option in its set that supplies its own causal clause ('eftersom kolhalten i metallen steg'), a form lean pointing the same way. C strips on 'Samtliga' and D on 'framfor allt' before any of this.
findings.why: Charged as a minor rather than waved through because the calibration argument that protects q3 and q4 -- that the deciding fact is specialist archaeometallurgy the passage exists to teach -- does not protect q2, where the deciding fact is school chemistry. Three verified mitigations keep it below blocker level: A is not the longest option (13 tokens against D's 17) and M-TELL passes; the causal-clause tell does not generalise across the sheet, because q3 carries causal markers on a distractor AND the key and q4 carries them on the key and two distractors, so 'pick the self-explaining option' resolves only q2; and the sheet's other blind channels actively misfire -- G-STEM's own blind solver got q1 WRONG on world knowledge (F9), so a domain-confident non-reader does not clean up. No action proposed on the bytes: the honest fix is the one G-STEM r1 already named (give B a parallel causal clause), and that is a repairer's call on a unit whose gate record is closed.

findings.stage_challenged: passage P6 (content) -- the 'sextiotva prover' spread the brief named
findings.disposition: RECORDED (no fix proposed; no key exposed)
findings.claim: P6 presents an inference as an entailment across two compressed steps: 'sextiotva prover fran elva ugnsplatser ... I dem lag jarnhalten i FLERA FALL kring en tredjedel av vikten, VILKET BETYDER ATT mer jarn stannade i avfallet an som lamnade ugnen i luppen.'
findings.evidence: Step one generalises an unquantified subset ('i flera fall' out of 62 samples) into a claim about the process. Step two converts a CONCENTRATION (Fe as a fraction of slag weight) into a MASS comparison (waste versus bloom), which strictly requires the slag:bloom mass ratio; the passage supplies that only obliquely and three paragraphs later ('Vid de fjorton platser som hittills matts in i socknen raknas varpen i ton', against 'En blasning gav nagra kilo jarn'). ~33 % Fe is squarely inside the real fayalitic range (fayalite is 54.8 % Fe; bloomery slags run 40-60 % FeO), and bloomery yields well under 50 % with slag mass exceeding bloom mass are the norm, so the conclusion is TRUE -- it is the 'vilket betyder att' that is doing unearned work.
findings.why: Recorded rather than charged because nothing hangs on it. No question tests the sample statistics; q4's key rests entirely on P7's two mechanism sentences ('En slagg med lagre jarnhalt blir trogflytande ...' and 'Jarnet i avfallet ar priset for att slaggen alls ska lamna schaktet'). The passage's own argumentative structure insulates it further: it leaves Krokvall's numbers standing and attacks only her inference, so the reported figures are never load-bearing for the key. A real facktext writer would hedge the same way. Noted so a future editorial pass can see it, not so anyone acts on it.

findings.disposition: RECORDED -- reconcilable; hunted specifically as a q3-A rescue and does not rescue it
findings.claim: P2 reports 1880s records of bogs 'tagits i bruk igen efter trettio eller fyrtio ar', while P9 dates 'bruket' to between the 300s and the 1200s. Read at speed, the first appears to place working in the 19th century and the second to exclude it.
findings.evidence: P2: 'Att skiktet kan bildas pa nytt ar kant sedan lange. I uppteckningar fran 1880-talet uppges samma mossar ha tagits i bruk igen efter trettio eller fyrtio ar.' P8 then definitises those records as the parish's own ('uppteckningarna, som ar utforliga om vem som agde vad'). P9: 'Kolet ur tappgroparna daterar bruket till tiden mellan 300-talet och 1200-talet.' The reconciliation is available and is historically the correct one: 'bruket' in P9 names the SMELTING, dated by charcoal from the tapping pits, while 'tagits i bruk' in P2 names ORE EXTRACTION from a bog, and 19th-century Swedish bog-ore digging fed the bruk, which is exactly the transition P5 describes ('Forst da flyttade tillverkningen fran socknarna till bruken'). The passage never says the 19th-century re-use was for bloomery smelting.
findings.why: Recorded because the brief asked for the hardest possible attack on q3, and this is the only textual foothold q3 A has for its 'langt in pa 1800-talet'. It is not enough: A also asserts that the districts supplied their OWN iron, which P5 and P2 both contradict, and A's causal claim ('den laga byggkostnaden gjorde att') elevates a one-paragraph sub-point over the text's stated hinge. G-KEY-r2B reached the same reading independently ('the 1880s records concern ore regrowth and ownership, not live smelting'). No fix proposed -- the ambiguity is the kind real facktext carries, and resolving it would cost the residue that law 9 wants.

Included because no gate in the fleet measures it and the owner should see that it was measured and found unthreatening rather than not measured at all.

findings.disposition: RECORDED, low confidence and low stakes; no fix proposed
findings.claim: 'rackning = upprepad upphettning och smidning som pressar ut slaggen ur luppen' folds two historically distinct stages into one term. In Swedish bruk terminology rackning primarily names the drawing-out of the smaltstycke into bar under a rackhammare, downstream of the consolidation/farskning stage that is where slag expulsion mainly happens.
findings.evidence: The passage itself uses the term for the consolidation work ('sedan maste den varmas och slas, gang pa gang, for att slaggen skulle pressas ur den' in P4, then 'i rackningen, dar ytterligare jarn forsvann vid varje varmning' in P5), and separately uses farska correctly for the pig-iron stage ('tackjarnet maste i sin tur farskas innan det gick att smida'). Swedish archaeometallurgical writing does apply rackning to bloom working, so the usage is defensible rather than wrong; it is the bruk-era term reaching backwards over a prehistoric process.
findings.why: Harmless to a student and structurally protected: the unit supplies its own gloss in-passage, and q3's key is licensed by the passage's own sentence ('Tyngdpunkten i arbetet lag inte vid ugnen utan i smedjan efterat, i rackningen'), not by outside terminology. Recorded only because a domain-expert reviewer might raise it and the audit should have already looked. Confidence deliberately marked low.

findings.disposition: GATE FINDING REFUTED -- recorded; no action needed on the unit
findings.claim: The G-STEM r1 major on q:1 records a WORLD_KNOWLEDGE leak with 'pick=A'. The shipped key is C. A blind channel that lands on a distractor is not a leak, and the domain claim the gate used to get there is itself wrong.
findings.evidence: The record reads: 'BLIND cont. A and C are contradictories on one axis ... Standard knowledge of myrmalm decides the pair: the ore was taken while the frost carried the mire. Domain knowledge is the deciding step, so flag.' Myrmalm was in fact lifted in late summer or autumn when the water in the mire had dropped, then heaped and left out so frost would break the lumps, and roasted afterwards -- which is exactly the passage's chain ('Arbetet gjordes sent pa hosten, nar vattnet i mossen hade sjunkit undan' ... 'fick ligga ute vintern over' ... 'Forst darefter rostades den'). Harvesting from the ice belongs to SJOMALM (lake ore); frozen-ground work in the myrmalm cycle is haulage, not lifting. The generator's own trap note anticipated this reader ('heavy winter haulage over frozen ground is real-world true ... so a knowledgeable solver is PULLED here'), and the gate's blind solver is the documented case of it working.
findings.why: Recorded rather than passed over because the prime directive is to refute, and refutation runs in both directions: a gate finding that would inflate the unit's residual count is as much a target as a generator claim. The net effect on the unit is favourable -- q1 is the one question on this sheet where domain confidence actively costs a non-reader the mark -- and that is what makes the q2 residual (F3) non-compounding. The G-STEM r1 q:1 flag should be reclassified from WORLD_KNOWLEDGE leak to 'world-knowledge trap fired as designed'. The record's OTHER q:1 observation, that 'Varje mosse' strips the field to three, is correct and is carried separately.
